about:
Universal Manufacturers was established in 1958 in the Kalihi neighborhood of Honolulu, Hawaii. The company began in the heart of Kalihi and has expanded over the decades into a full-service fabrication operation. The business is run family-style by second-generation kamaʻaina—local residents—who have kept ownership in the family since its founding.

Today the company operates a fully equipped metal fabrication shop that works with all metals and thicknesses. Its capabilities include structural components, custom metal parts, and food service equipment, though the facility’s square footage, employee count, and production volumes are not publicly specified. The company states its intent to provide premium metal fabrication and related services across the State of Hawaii.

The firm’s project portfolio highlights food service equipment as a notable specialty, suggesting a focus on the hospitality and food service sectors. Its website lists fabricated products and structural components as primary outputs. No additional industries are explicitly named in the available information.

Leadership points to more than 60 years of combined fabrication experience among management personnel as the foundation for efficient, quality work on every job. This experience base is cited as a key reason the firm can maintain efficiency and quality across diverse projects.
